item.title: TCP vs. UDP in .NET: Speed, Reliability, and the Hidden Cost of Performance
item.description: Choosing between TCP and UDP is crucial for data transport. TCP ensures reliability and ordered delivery, making it ideal for critical applications, while UDP prioritizes speed and low latency, suited for real-time scenarios. Link to article: https://dotnettips.com/2026/07/19/tcp-vs-udp-in-net-speed-reliability-and-the-hidden-cost-of-performance/

item.title: Optimizing I/O Performance in .NET
item.description: I/O operations impact application responsiveness, scalability, and costs. Enhancing file access, HTTP requests, and networking improves user experience while reducing resource consumption. This chapter discusses techniques to optimize I/O performance in .NET, utilizing benchmark results and profilers to identify bottlenecks and improve efficiency in near-production environments. Link to article: https://dotnettips.com/2026/07/12/optimizing-i-o-performance-in-net/

item.title: HTTP/3 in .NET: Faster, Newer, and Not Always the Best Choice
item.description: Modern .NET applications support three major HTTP versions: HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, and HTTP/3, each with distinct characteristics. HTTP/3, utilizing QUIC over UDP, offers advantages like reduced latency and better performance on unstable networks. Link to article: https://dotnettips.com/2026/07/12/http-3-in-net-faster-newer-and-not-always-the-best-choice/
